A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

MPO-ANCAs are a useful marker for WG, especially in patients with cranial pachy-meningitis, and that HCP should be considered as a possible complication of MPO-AN-Ca-associated vasculitis, even in the absence of other systemic manifestations of WG.

The main takeaway from our work is that
HCP is an uncommon but potentially serious manifestation of WG.
MPO-ANCAs should be considered in the workup of patients with HCP, especially in the presence of multiple cranial nerve deficits and/or granuloma-like lesions.
HCP should be included in the differential diagnosis of patients with WG, and MPO-ANCa should be considered as one of the diagnostic criteria for WG.
